items.q: In the Couinaud anatomical segmentation of the liver, which independent segment receives vascular inflow from both left and right portal branches and drains directly into the inferior vena cava?
items.exp: Segment I (caudate lobe) is functionally distinct: it receives blood from both right and left portal triads and drains directly into the IVC via independent hepatic veins, often hypertrophy in Budd-Chiari syndrome.
r: Correct. Segment I (caudate lobe) receives dual portal inflow and drains directly into the IVC.
Incorrect. Segment IV is part of the left functional liver.
Incorrect. Segment II is the superior lateral left segment.
Incorrect. Segment VIII is the anterosuperior right segment.
items.kp: Couinaud segment I (caudate lobe) receives dual portal inflow and drains directly into the IVC, sparing it in hepatic vein thrombosis.

items.q: Which structures constitute the classic portal triad enclosed within the hepatoduodenal ligament at the porta hepatis?
o: Proper hepatic artery, portal vein, and common bile duct
Hepatic vein, portal vein, and celiac trunk
Inferior vena cava, splenic vein, and cystic duct
Celiac trunk, hepatic vein, and gastroduodenal artery
items.exp: The portal triad consists of the proper hepatic artery, hepatic portal vein, and common bile duct, contained within the free edge of the lesser omentum (hepatoduodenal ligament).
r: Correct. The portal triad contains the proper hepatic artery, portal vein, and common bile duct.
Incorrect. Hepatic veins drain superiorly into the IVC.
Incorrect. IVC is retroperitoneal.
Incorrect. Celiac trunk is on the posterior abdominal wall.
items.kp: The portal triad within the hepatoduodenal ligament comprises the portal vein, proper hepatic artery, and common bile duct.

items.q: In hepatic microarchitecture, which cell type located in the space of Disse is responsible for vitamin A storage in health and excessive collagen deposition during liver cirrhosis?
items.exp: Hepatic stellate cells (Ito cells) reside in the space of Disse. They store vitamin A in quiescence, but under inflammatory stimulation transdifferentiate into collagen-secreting myofibroblasts, driving fibrosis.
r: Correct. Stellate cells store vitamin A and synthesize collagen in cirrhosis.
Incorrect. Kupffer cells are resident tissue macrophages.
Incorrect. Endothelial cells line the sinusoids.
Incorrect. Hepatocytes perform metabolic and secretory duties.
items.kp: Hepatic stellate cells in the space of Disse store vitamin A and become myofibroblasts that drive liver fibrosis and cirrhosis.

items.q: According to Rappaport hepatic acinar zoning, which metabolic zone surrounds the central vein and is most vulnerable to ischemic necrosis and toxic acetaminophen injury?
items.exp: Zone 3 (centrilobular) is farthest from incoming portal arterioles, having the lowest oxygen tension and the highest cytochrome P450 concentration, making it most vulnerable to ischemia and toxic injury.
r: Correct. Zone 3 has the lowest oxygen tension and highest P450 concentration, making it vulnerable to ischemia and acetaminophen toxicity.
Incorrect. Zone 1 is best oxygenated and resists ischemia.
Incorrect. Zone 2 is an intermediate transition zone.
Incorrect. Space of Mall is at the portal tract border.
items.kp: Acinar Zone 3 (centrilobular) is most susceptible to ischemic injury and toxic metabolite damage from high CYP450 activity.

items.q: What percentage of total hepatic blood flow is normally delivered by the hepatic portal vein?
items.exp: The portal vein delivers approximately 75% of blood flow to the liver (rich in nutrients from the GI tract), while the hepatic artery delivers the remaining 25% (high in oxygen).
r: Correct. The portal vein supplies approximately 75% of hepatic blood volume.
Incorrect. Hepatic artery provides about 25% of flow.
Incorrect. Flow is not equally split.
Incorrect. Arterial perfusion is mandatory for biliary epithelium.
items.kp: The portal vein supplies roughly 75% of hepatic blood flow, while the hepatic artery supplies the remaining 25%.

items.q: The ligamentum teres hepatis (round ligament) running in the free edge of the falciform ligament represents the fibrous remnant of which fetal vascular structure?
items.exp: The round ligament of the liver (ligamentum teres) is the obliterated fibrous cord of the left umbilical vein, which carried oxygenated placental blood to the fetal liver.
r: Correct. Ligamentum teres is the obliterated remnant of the left umbilical vein.
Incorrect. Ductus venosus obliterates to form ligamentum venosum.
Incorrect. Umbilical arteries obliterate to form medial umbilical ligaments.
Incorrect. Ductus arteriosus forms ligamentum arteriosum.
items.kp: The ligamentum teres hepatis is the anatomical remnant of the obliterated fetal left umbilical vein.

items.q: In cirrhotic portal hypertension, opening of portosystemic collateral veins between the left gastric vein and esophageal veins leads to which life-threatening complication?
items.exp: Left gastric (coronary) veins anastomose with esophageal branches of the azygos vein at the lower esophagus, forming fragile submucosal esophageal varices that can bleed catastrophically.
r: Correct. Anastomosis between left gastric and azygos veins forms bleeding esophageal varices.
Incorrect. Caput medusae forms via paraumbilical veins on anterior abdominal wall.
Incorrect. Retroperitoneal collaterals involve veins of Retzius.
Incorrect. Hemorrhoids involve superior and inferior rectal veins.
items.kp: Portosystemic collaterals between the left gastric vein and azygos esophageal veins form life-threatening esophageal varices.

items.q: Which plane demarcates the functional anatomical division between the true left liver and right liver, passing from the gallbladder fossa to the inferior vena cava?
items.exp: Cantlie line (the principal portal scissura) runs from the gallbladder fossa anteriorly to the middle of the IVC posteriorly, dividing the liver into functional left and right lobes.
r: Correct. Cantlie line divides the functional right and left liver based on vascular inflow.
Incorrect. Falciform ligament marks anatomical superficial division, not the functional plane.
Incorrect. Left triangular ligament attaches segment II to diaphragm.
Incorrect. Umbilical fissure separates segment III from segment IV.
items.kp: Cantlie line extends from the gallbladder fossa to the IVC, defining the functional border between right and left hemiliver.

items.q: Resident tissue macrophages lining the fenestrated hepatic sinusoids that phagocytose circulating debris and aged erythrocytes are called:
items.exp: Kupffer cells are specialized resident macrophages that adhere to sinusoidal endothelial luminal surfaces, clearing bacteria, endotoxins, and damaged erythrocytes from portal blood.
r: Correct. Kupffer cells are the resident sinusoidal macrophages of the liver.
Incorrect. Ito cells are stellate cells in the space of Disse.
Incorrect. Fenestrations are physical endothelial pores.
Incorrect. Hepatocytes are parenchymal epithelial cells.
items.kp: Kupffer cells are liver-resident macrophages lining the sinusoids that clear particulate antigens and bacteria from portal flow.

items.q: Biliary epithelium lining intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts is vascularized almost exclusively by which arterial source, predisposing to ischemic cholangiopathy if damaged during transplantation?
o: Peribiliary plexus derived from the hepatic artery
items.exp: Bile duct epithelial cells depend entirely on the peribiliary vascular plexus supplied by the hepatic artery. Hepatic artery thrombosis after liver transplantation causes ischemic biliary necrosis and strictures.
r: Correct. Biliary epithelium relies entirely on the arterial peribiliary plexus.
Incorrect. Portal venous blood is deoxygenated and cannot sustain biliary tree viability.
Incorrect. Venous plexuses do not provide arterial perfusion.
Incorrect. Short gastric vessels supply the stomach.
items.kp: Bile duct epithelium depends entirely on the hepatic arterial peribiliary plexus; arterial thrombosis causes biliary strictures.
